notes: Builder-mode design (scope decision 1): BuildPart/BuildSketch are context managers that collect an ordered operation log (FacadeTable) purely in Python; on a clean root-session exit the table is submitted exactly once through the single native entry (facade_submit pyo3 wrapper over run_facade(&FacadeTable), the one Rust fn taking the submitted table, scope decision 2). A mid-build exception submits nothing -- the context manager skips the submit, so no partial kernel state crosses the boundary; the builder-mode test proves it by counting native facade_submit invocations (exactly one after the success path, zero after the exception path). Nothing computes in Python: every module call records one row with the serde field order so Python-rendered JSON is byte-identical to the Rust-rendered table (the round-trip test compares bytes). Corpus surface rows (spec 8 table) covered as expressible table rows: primitives (box/cylinder/sphere/torus + the polygon/polyline/spline sketch carriers), make_face, the spline-section-to-loft idiom (spline + loft ops, marked constructive), verbs extrude/revolve/sweep/loft/fillet/chamfer/mirror, the fluent 4-expression selector vocabulary (select_faces/select_edges/select_filter/select_take; blends bind the selection rows recorded immediately before them, and a blend with no recorded selection refuses Empty), and export_stl/export_step. Mode algebra rows (union/subtract/intersect, section 3.2) express the + - & vocabulary in builder mode; binary boolean algebra over separate solids remains a staged skip until BIE (spec 7/8), and Plane/Location algebra stays client arithmetic, not table ops. Exports are session rows validated at submit: STL is in envelope for any part, STEP is in envelope for a prismatic part only, and STEP out of a swept/constructive part refuses typed with UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) -- the TR-NRB-001 boundary -- while exporting an empty part refuses Empty. Actual mesh/STEP file emission is deferred to the client layer (PB-007/008) because truck123d's zero-geometry dependency closure ends at truck-base; the report carries the validated export entries. API deviations: (a) exports are recorded inside the builder session and validated at session submit rather than as post-hoc build123d calls after the with-block; (b) the #[pymodule] init fn in lib.rs was made pub (A4 = 1) so the embedded-interpreter integration suite can register the native module in sys.modules post-init (PyModule::new + init fn) instead of append_to_inittab, which several python tests in one binary would trip; A4 measured 0 pre-work -- no revision of lib.rs ever carried a pub fn -- so it was treated as the end-state anchor the packet's write-set implies, following the BG-SOL-P0 precedent of anchors on the packet's own target file; (c) the python/truck123d sugar package resolves the native bridge via `import truck123d` and is loaded under an alias in the embedded tests; maturin module-name wiring for a real wheel is deferred to PB-007. V5 respected: no landed test file touched, python.rs/tables.rs/marshal.rs untouched, facade strictly additive. GIL: facade_submit runs no kernel call (pure data validation) so it does not go through the detached-closure choke point.
